kicker: A new peak rises every week. Who measured how high it is?
summary: AI news arrives every week, and some models are not open to everyone. When news comes, ask: who measured, and who checked again?

quiz.q: A company says its new model is so capable it is not being released to everyone. What should you ask first?
options: Has anyone outside checked that claim?
Is the new model bigger than the last one?
Is the company's demo video impressive?
Are lots of experts speaking up to praise it?
quiz.explain: “So capable it needs a fence” is the company's own word. Bigger, a nice demo, praising experts are not proof; Mozilla fixing 271 bugs is a check from outside.

peaks.label: The peaks
peaks.art: You stand on a mossy rock ridge above a valley full of cloud. A big moon has just risen on the right. Five pointed rock peaks rise out of the sea of cloud on an arc, their shadows lying long to the left across it. On each crown sits a low stone slab carved with one model launch, in date order from left to right, joined by a fine broken stroke of ink. From here all five look the same height. A leaning pine stands on the left, a stone lantern on the right.
peaks.prompt: Touch a stele, then light the lantern
steps: Light the stone lantern: keep only what was checked
Put the lantern out to look again, or go on
peaks.hint: Drag to look around. Touch a peak to turn its stele, touch the stone lantern to keep only what someone outside has checked, press Esc to come back.
peaks.sky: Each peak: an AI model launched in 2026
peaks.group: Steles for the new models, in order of release date
peaks.verifiedOnly: Light it: keep only what outsiders have checked
peaks.verifiedOnlyAria: Light the stone lantern: keep only what someone outside has checked
peaks.litNote: Most numbers on these steles were measured by the makers themselves — nobody outside has measured them again.

checked.n-2026-04-deepseek-v4: Open weights: anyone can download and test it

insight.text: Five companies launched new models within a few months. The steles give only date and source, because nobody outside has measured who is better.

peaks.detail: Grok (xAI), Qwen (Alibaba) and Mistral have big models too; AI Zen has not yet checked their latest releases, so no steles stand for them.

gate.label: The fenced summit
gate.art: Eye level, right against the bamboo fence on the highest summit. A few blurred bamboo stalks at the edges; in the middle a gate of two latticed wooden doors, barred by a wooden bolt. Through the lattice, lamplight inside: a wall laid in lines of code, a red crack, two workers patching it, two stone lanterns, twelve small lamps along the wall and, further off, a faint band of lights. Behind the wall rise the summit, the moon and the mist. On the left, by a small wicket in the fence, a man with a lantern waits.
gate.prompt: Try sliding the bolt to the right
gate.gateAria: Try sliding the wooden bolt to the right to open the gate (or press Enter)
gate.jammed: This gate is not open to you.
steps: Look at the small gate: who gets in?
gate.keeperAria: The man with the lantern at the small gate: see who gets in
gate.allowed: In first: Apple, AWS, the Linux Foundation and more than 40 organisations that maintain critical software

reason.text: Anthropic says Mythos finds software flaws so well that attackers could use it too, so it goes first to the people who fix them.

gate.courtPrompt: Touch the lantern bearer at each gate
gate.courtArt: Looking down on the fenced summit floating in the sea of cloud, like a temple ground plan. A raked gravel court in the middle, four gates at the four quarters. Outside each gate stand a lantern bearer and a carved sign: the gate itself, a stone with fresh mortar, a stone with a single notch, a smaller fenced ring. Open a gate and its bearer walks to the middle of the court, leaving footprints.

view.text: The company says Mythos found thousands of flaws nobody knew about, in every major operating system and browser.

stones.who: Mozilla · maker of the Firefox browser (05/2026)

view.text: Mozilla confirms: it fixed 271 bugs found by Mythos, 180 of them urgent.
In mid-April, before Mozilla's report, VulnCheck could count only 1 officially published flaw tied to the project.
OpenAI is also opening GPT-6 Astra only gradually, first to selected customers, because it worries about the model's hacking ability.

common.text: Everyone sees AI has become very good at finding flaws. Still argued: who gets to use it first, and who checks the company's word.

insight.text: In 2026, some AI models are not released to everyone. The company hands them first to the people who fix software flaws.

detail.text: The project is called Glasswing, announced 7 April 2026. The vulnerability counts come from the company and its partners themselves.

stele.label: Reading the stele without being fooled
stele.art: A large stone stele under a pavilion roof, carved with a mock press release in big letters. The visitor sweeps a paper lantern across it: in the lantern light, five faint carvings appear beside the loudest sentences.
stele.prompt: Shine the lantern on each advertising line
stele.lanternAria: Sweep the lantern over the stele, or use Tab to move through each sentence and press Enter
stele.mockTitle: PRESS RELEASE · Launching the Shooting Star model

mockNote.text: The press release and the “Shooting Star” model are mock-ups written by AI Zen for practising how to read the news.

lines.text: Shooting Star beats EVERY rival on 12 benchmarks!
lines.question: Did the company score itself, or did someone outside? With which test, under what conditions?
lines.aria: Inspect: beats every rival on 12 benchmarks

lines.text: Watch: Shooting Star builds an app in 30 seconds.
lines.question: Is the video the best run out of how many tries? Have you tried it on your own work?
lines.aria: Inspect: video of an app built in 30 seconds

lines.text: Technical details will be published later.
lines.question: Has the company published a document saying plainly where the model is weak and what the risks are?
lines.aria: Inspect: technical details will be published later

lines.text: Available to everyone from today*  (*premium plan, usage limits apply)
lines.question: Who can really use it, at what price, and how many times a day?
lines.aria: Inspect: available to everyone from today, with a small asterisk

lines.question: Which experts — are they named? Have researchers, reputable press or real users checked it yet?
lines.aria: Inspect: experts rate it very highly

stele.done: All 5 caught — take the card from the stele's base

insight.text: The biggest line is the one the company wants you to remember. The small print tells who measured, what it costs, who checked.

detail.text: Even when launching Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic wrote that in real use the gap with another of its models is smaller than the scores suggest. Scoreboards (benchmarks) don't tell the whole story.

tide.label: The release tide
tide.art: Lying at the water’s edge at one end of a long tidal flat that runs diagonally into the distance, to a mountain with cloud round its summit: time runs into depth. The tide is in, water covers the flat and the moon’s broken road runs toward you. Drag the moon across the sky and the water draws back toward the mountain while the stones rise in date order: far apart near you, crowding at the mountain’s foot and climbing its flank like steps.
tide.prompt: Drag the moon to the right
tide.promptToday: Look up at the summit in the cloud
tide.moonAria: Drag the moon, or use the ← → keys to move through the milestones
tide.stones: Each stone: one AI model at GPT-4 size or larger (as counted by Epoch AI)

fact.text: OpenAI introduces ChatGPT, letting anyone chat with a large language model.
GPT-4 (03/2023) was the first model trained with a huge amount of computing — Epoch AI uses it as the mark for “large”.
Throughout 2024, about two models at that scale were announced each month on average.
By June 2025, Epoch AI counted more than 30 models at GPT-4 scale or above, from 12 developers.
Anthropic announces Claude Mythos Preview but does not release it widely, giving it only to organisations that find and fix security flaws.
Between 21 July and 28 September 2026, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic released four new models — in under ten weeks.

horizon.text: The pace of releases may keep quickening — but that is a guess; no one can see through the clouds on the summit yet.

insight.text: In early 2023 there was 1 model at GPT-4 size. By mid-2025 there were over 30, from 12 companies.

detail: Bigger is not always better. But the more companies can build large models, the more “beats every rival” headlines arrive.
No reliable source counts releases per quarter, so the stones use Epoch AI's count of large models (measured by the computing used in training, FLOP).

anthropic-glasswing.note: Official page: Claude Mythos Preview goes only to defensive partners and is not planned for wide release. The vulnerability counts are self-reported by the company and its partners.

epoch-1e25.note: Figures as of June 2025 (major update on 6 June 2025); the number today is probably higher.

mozilla-mythos.title: Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox with Claude Mythos Preview
mozilla-mythos.note: Mozilla is a user, not the model's maker. Firefox 150 fixed 271 bugs found by Mythos Preview: 180 high, 80 moderate, 11 low. Mozilla notes the ratings measure urgency, not proof of exploitation.

cso-glasswing.title: Behind the Mythos hype, Glasswing has just one confirmed CVE
cso-glasswing.note: Cites VulnCheck's analysis (Patrick Garrity). Written before Mozilla's report of 7 May 2026.

bleeping-gpt6.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra can find zero-days, but is also harder to monitor
bleeping-gpt6.note: Quotes OpenAI's system card: GPT-6 Astra reaches the “Critical” cybersecurity threshold under the company's own framework. OpenAI's original page blocks lookup tools, so it has not been opened directly.
